# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen`. Edit the command catalog or CLI registration instead. -->

Use `board <command> --help` for interactive help. `--json` is available globally and on catalog operations; direct binary routes accept no extra arguments.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                            |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success.                                                                           |
| 1    | Refused or a blocking doctor check.                                                |
| 2    | Invalid command, arguments, or flags.                                              |
| 3    | A dependency prevented the action; it did not apply.                               |
| 4    | Configuration or installation failure.                                             |
| 5    | The action may have applied; inspect the result before retrying with the same key. |

## Daemon address and caller identity

Catalog commands, `board token create` and MCP tool calls reach the daemon at `BOARD_DAEMON_URL`, otherwise at `http://127.0.0.1:<http.port>` from `config.yaml`. With `BOARD_DAEMON_URL` unset and `config.yaml` missing, malformed or invalid, they stop with `config` (exit 4) before sending anything; the error names both. Set `BOARD_DAEMON_URL`, or fix `config.yaml` and set `http.port`; `board doctor --offline` names what is wrong. `BOARD_DAEMON_URL` may use `http:` only on a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`); any other host needs `https:`, because the token or session is sent with each call. Catalog commands, `board token create`, MCP tool calls, `board update` and `board rollback` refuse a plain-http address on another host with `config` (exit 4) before sending anything, and the error does not repeat the address.

The caller is `SPUR_SESSION` inside a Spur session, otherwise `BOARD_TOKEN`, otherwise the first `.spur-board/token` found walking upward from the working directory. The walk stops at the root of the git worktree (the first folder with a `.git` file or directory, which is still searched); outside git it stops before home. Home itself is never searched, even when it is the worktree root. A token above the worktree root, or in home, is not used: move it into a folder inside the worktree or set `BOARD_TOKEN`.

Inside a Spur session the session wins over a token: `SPUR_SESSION` is sent and neither `BOARD_TOKEN` nor `.spur-board/token` is read. A session whose Spur project is in no `projects[].spurProjects` or top-level `spurProjects` of the Board's `config.yaml`, or is listed under several Board projects, is refused with `forbidden` (exit 1), and the hint names the Spur project and the fix.

## Why a task waits

`board task <task> --why` starts with `why.waitsFor`: what the task waits for and who acts next. On a terminal its first line is `waits for: <text>`. `text` ends with the actor in parentheses when one acts next, `actor` is that role, `human` for a person on GitHub, or null when the board, GitHub or Spur settles it. An enabled Done gate of a task not in Done, and the To Do group gate of the column a task sits in before work starts, carry a `waitsFor` text too. On a terminal `--why` leaves out the gates of disabled columns; `--all` lists them. `--json` and output that is not a terminal always list every column.

| `waitsFor.kind` | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `turn`          | An open turn: `Review turn T4 (orchestrator:review)`; `actor` is its addressee.                                                                                                      |
| `merge`         | A human merges the PR: `merge of acme/web#42 (a human)`.                                                                                                                             |
| `approval`      | A human approval on GitHub: an external review, required reviewers, the review rule or a new review after requested changes.                                                         |
| `ticket`        | The ticket closes: `ticket to close` after a merge, or `ticket to close, with no open PR and no live worker`.                                                                        |
| `checks`        | CI on the head: `CI on <sha8>` or `green checks on <sha8>`.                                                                                                                          |
| `github`        | GitHub to be readable, or to compute mergeability, the merge state or the review rule.                                                                                               |
| `spur`          | Spur to be readable.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `board`         | The board: the first poll of the PR, a submit confirmation, the full comment history or the next dispatcher pass.                                                                    |
| `answer`        | An answer to the blocks of an open cycle-limit or course-check item: `answer to B4 (curator)`.                                                                                       |
| `work`          | Work to start in the To Do group, `work to start: an open PR or a live worker` (only an open PR after a reopen), or a worker session to end before a done ticket completes the task. |
| `gate`          | The column's exit conditions: `Review exit: no_review_on_head`.                                                                                                                      |
| `done`          | Nothing: the task is done.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `archived`      | Nothing while the task is archived: the dispatcher skips it; unarchive it to resume. No gate carries a `waitsFor` text.                                                              |
| `config`        | The project is gone from `config.yaml`: `the project in config.yaml (operator)`.                                                                                                     |

`board task <task> --why --json` lists in `waiting` each fact the task waits for, with its gate reason, the PR head in `head` and a one-line `text`. The texts depend on the project's `checksGate`:

| Reason                       | `checksGate: dev` (default)                                          | Another `checksGate` column                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checks_pending`             | `waiting for CI on <sha>`                                            | `checks running, exit from <checksGate> waits for green`                                                         |
| `checks_red`                 | not listed: the task returns to Dev                                  | `checks red`, listed whenever red checks keep the task in Dev or a taken turn holds it in place until its submit |
| `mergeable_unknown`          | `waiting for GitHub to compute mergeability on <sha>`                | the same                                                                                                         |
| `comment_history_incomplete` | `waiting for the board to read the full PR comment history on <sha>` | the same                                                                                                         |

Under a `checksGate` other than `dev`, Dev's gate lists `checks_not_red` instead of `checks_green`, and the `checksGate` column lists `checks_green` first. A cancelled check there reads `checks_pending` until two complete GitHub polls after the one that saw it, then `checks_red`.

With `approvalRule: github-rules` on External Review only, its gate also lists `review_rule_satisfied`, and `waiting` can carry five more reasons, none with the sha:

| Reason                        | Text                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `review_rule_blocked`         | `merge blocked by the GitHub review rule`                                    |
| `awaiting_required_reviewers` | `awaiting required reviewers: <login>, <slug>`, the list also in `reviewers` |
| `changes_requested`           | `changes requested`                                                          |
| `merge_state_unknown`         | `GitHub has not computed the merge state yet`                                |
| `review_rule_unreadable`      | `the GitHub review rule for the base branch could not be read`               |

### `board mcp`

Start the MCP server for an agent on standard input and output. Stdout carries only JSON-RPC.

Each tool call finds the caller: `SPUR_SESSION` inside a Spur session, otherwise `BOARD_TOKEN`, otherwise the first `.spur-board/token` found walking upward from the directory the agent starts it in, stopping at the root of its git worktree, or at home outside git; home itself is never searched.

It reaches the daemon at `BOARD_DAEMON_URL`, otherwise at `http.port` from `config.yaml`; with neither set nor a valid config, each call fails with `config` before any request.

A `version_mismatch` answer means the server and the daemon have different catalogs: restart the agent session so `board mcp` loads the daemon's catalog; if it remains, run `board service restart`.

Register it with Claude Code: `claude mcp add spur-board -- board mcp`. With Codex: `codex mcp add spur-board -- board mcp`.

Arguments: none.

Flags:

None.

Example: `board mcp`

Exit codes: see the table above; setup errors are reported by the CLI.

### `board status`

List items, freshness, service health, host metrics, tasks with columnEnteredAt, turns and PRs; detail adds facts.

Arguments: none.

Flags:

`--project <value>` — Project to limit the answer to, except sources and services, which always cover every project the caller may see; absent means every project the caller may see.
`--detail` — Include full ticket, pull request and session facts; absent means compact rows.
`--json` — Print JSON output or a JSON error.

Example: `board status`

### `board task`

Show a task; refresh reads GitHub PRs.

Arguments: `<task>`.

Flags:

`--refresh` — Read every linked pull request from GitHub before showing the task; unavailable reads fail visibly.
`--detail` — Also list the last 5 closed turns, newest first; absent means none.
`--why` — Explain why the task is in its column: what it waits for, gates, holds, the open turn and the last moves; absent means no explanation.
`--all` — With --why on a terminal, also list the gates of disabled columns; JSON always lists every column.
`--json` — Print JSON output or a JSON error.

Example: `board task PROJ-123`

### `board wait`

Wait on a turn the caller took for what the Board cannot see; the Board stays quiet, then rings the holder when the wait ends. The operator can end the active wait early.

Arguments: `<turn>`.

Flags:

`--for <value>` — Whole minutes to wait, 1 to 120; the turn total cap may shorten it. Required unless end.
`--reason <value>` — What you wait for, up to 200 characters; the wake ring repeats it. Required unless end. Wait only on what the Board cannot see: a busy test stand, no free slot, high machine load, someone else's deploy, an outside service you call. Not on your own work (review fixes, tests, checks, rebasing): work holding the turn, so a stall reaches the operator; a wait hides it. Not on what the Board watches (CI runs in any state, reviews, approvals, mergeability, merges): submit the head and stop; red checks or other needs bring a new Dev turn. If your next step needs it (you merge, or shadow mode), wait for it.
`--end` — Operator only: end the turn's active wait now instead of starting one; pass no for or reason.
`--key <key>` — Idempotency key for this action.
`--json` — Print JSON output or a JSON error.

Example: `board wait T4 --for 30 --reason "waiting for a free test stand" --key wait-PROJ-123-example-1432`

`--json` — Print JSON output or a JSON error.

Example: `board order PROJ-123 --before PROJ-120 --key order-PROJ-123-example-1432`

Operation errors: `usage` (exit 2: Run `board schema` to see the expected input and fix the arguments.); `wrong_id_kind` (exit 2: Pass the ID kind the operation expects, e.g. B<n> for a block or a task key for a task.); `forbidden` (exit 1: Check which role may run the operation in `board schema`, or ask the operator.); `not_found` (exit 1: Check the ID with `board status` or `board task <KEY>`.); `not_implemented` (exit 1: Ask the operator to update the daemon to a build with this operation.); `order_anchor_invalid` (exit 1: Pick another task from the same column in `board status`, or use `--top` or `--bottom`.); `task_archived` (exit 1: Ask an operator to add the task to the board again if work continues.); `idempotency_key_mismatch` (exit 1: Use a new key for a new command, or repeat the earlier input with the same key.); `identity_unavailable` (exit 3: Ask in your own session, then retry the same command later with its existing idempotency key if it has one.); `starting` (exit 3: Wait until the daemon is ready, then retry the command with its existing idempotency key if it has one.); `stopping` (exit 3: Wait until the daemon is running again, then retry the command with its existing idempotency key if it has one; if it stays stopped, ask in your own session.).
